SKIN. [46] [Con.]
Blueness of whole body.
Yellow color of skin ; jaundice.
Yellow spots on fingers ; yellow nails.
Brown spots upon body.
Want of action of skin.
Erratic itching of all parts of body, as from fleas.
Itching on dorsum of finger.
Itching < by scratching.
Urticaria, from violent bodily exercise.
Eruptions developed by being overheated.
Inflammation of skin all over body ; painful and burning.
White transparent pimples filled with an acrid humor, which forms scabs resembling those of scabies.
A man, æt. 73, fell out of buggy ; bruises on left arm, formed a scab, left a scar, surrounded by an induration which burned and itched. Con. [30] reduced the induration to one-third in a week, softened the remainder, and helped markedly an involuntary mucous diarrhœa, jelly-like, white, inodorous, at times slimy, almost white, a dozen or more stools daily, so that he has now regular passages, also had incontinence of urine which is >.
Glandular enlargement ; moist vesicles, < by scratching, followed by pricking in skin ; gluey, sticky discharge, forming hard crusts about face, arms and mons veneris ; eruptions in old people suffering from vertigo, especially in bed.
Sudden herpetic eruption on forearm, beginning as a small spot and gradually spreading over arm ; skin red, swollen and corrugated, lymph or blood oozing from broken places in skin, lymph drying and forming white crusts under which the exudation still continues ; intense itching in affected parts, with irresistible desire to scratch, particularly in evening ; surrounding lymphatics swollen and involved.
Herpetic eruption forming into scabs as large as hand in various parts of body.
Acne on face.
Tetters : humid, burning, corroding, crusty, old.
Sero-purulent eruption in aged people, and hypochondriacal old maids.
Petechia in old persons.
Tumor can be traced to a bruise ; lancinating pains.
Adenitis.
Blackish ulcers, with bloody, fetid, ichorous discharges, especially after contusions.
Ulcers : cancerous ; scabby ; destitute of feeling ; with tight, tense feeling ; speckled.
Scurfy exanthema ; polypus ; greenish mortification ; tetters in general.
Edges of ulcer become black ; gangrene of parts of ulcer ; creeping, with a tensive pain ; ulcers which are bluish have a livid appearance and are tumid ; pain in part as if it was beaten to pieces ; swollen ulcers, hard to heal ; inflamed ulcers, with a feeling of soreness.
Bleeding from ulcers.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Con.]
Cannot take alcoholic stimulants ; easily intoxicated.
Strong persons of a sedentary habit are affected more than lively and slender persons and children.
Suited to women of rigid fibre, easily excited, as well as to those of opposite temperament.
Hypochondriacal old maids ; old, weak and feeble men.
Especially useful to old people, and among these to women more than to men.
Light-haired persons.
Debility of old people ; diseases caused by a blow or fall ; cancerous and scrofulous people, with tight rigid fibre.
Scrofulous constitutions ; strumous condition, enlarged glands.
Apoplectic paralysis.
Children who are prematurely old ; with marasmus, with frequent sour evacuations, < during night, > by day.
Girl, æt. 4 ; diphtheria after scarlatina.
HS., æt. 4 1/2, had jaundice two years ago ; ophthalmia.
Girl, æt. 6, of scrofulous constitution, had suffered for a long time from ulcer on right great toe, which had healed up for ten months ; she had also cicatrix resulting from suppuration of glands on neck and lower jaw ; seven months after healing of ulcer, inflammation of eyes.
Girl, æt. 10 ; cough.
Boy, æt. 13, noise in larynx, with twitching of muscles of face ; allopathic treatment of no avail ; Bellad. given without result ; under old school treatment had received Conium without effect.
Young man, æt. 16, strong and healthy ; derangement of mind.
Girl, æt. 16, tissues flabby, scrofulous, menstruated one year ; swelling of lids.
Young lady, æt. 18, lymphatic, scrofulous constitution ; photophobia.
Susanna F., æt. 19, robust, of slender form, perfectly developed, affected from infancy with ophthalmia ; inflammation of eyes.
Robust girl, æt. 20, suffering formerly from swelling of lymphatics and eruptions on head ; herpetic eruption.
Woman, æt. 22, delicate, but healthy ; for five years after contusion scirrhus of left breast.
Miss G., æt. 25, has always had dysmenorrhœa ; prolapsus and dysmenorrhœa.
Girl, æt. 26 ; suffering since childhood from herpes.
Woman, æt. 27, pale, scrofulous appearance ; cramps in stomach during pregnancy.
Miss A. P., æt. 28 ; dysmenorrhœa.
Woman, æt. 30, otherwise healthy ; half year after contusion of right breast, tumor.
Ammon S., æt. 32, well developed, strong looking, five feet four inches in height, sick with peritonitis after having for a year felt tired and overworked, convalescence slow and protracted ; anemic state of brain.
Woman, æt. 33, married ; uterine disorder.
Mrs. B., æt. 35, fell, striking right breast on back of chair, causing a hard tumor.
Young man, tuberculous, after attack of catarrh ; dry, tickling cough.
Young man, after falling from second story upon back ; pain in lower part of back and in region of small of back.
Lady, accomplished, lively ; melancholia.
Strong, corpulent woman ; scirrhus in mamma.
Woman, weak, excitable ; galactorrhœa.
Mrs. G., æt. about 40 ; tumor of left breast of six or seven years standing.
Mrs. F., æt. 40 ; tumor on breast.
Edward S., a Russian, æt. 45, formerly soldier in United States army, and under allopathic treatment ; dysentery of four years' standing.
Woman, æt. 48 ; vertigo.
Woman, æt. 48, nervous constitution ; enlargement of liver.
A. man, æt. 48 ; first threatened softening of brain, helped by Laches., then right-sided paralysis, particularly facial, helped by Caustic., afterwards diabetes mellitus of two years' standing, with swelling and suppuration of left parotid and profuse sweat with insomnia.
Woman, æt. 54, plethoric ; uterine polypi.
Mrs. S. R., æt. 54, and Mrs. C. N., æt. 62 ; scirrhous cancer of breast.
Man, æt. 60 ; after injury to eye by a splinter of wood, traumatic inflammation.
Woman, æt. 60 ; cancer of stomach.
Lady, æt. 67, unmarried ; cough.
Woman, æt. 74, paralyzed many years on left side ; cough.
Mrs. ---, æt. 75 ; pain in chest during pneumonia.
   

RELATIONS. [48] [Con.]
Antidoted by : Coffea, Dulcam., Nitr. ac., Nitr. spir. dulc.
It antidotes : Mercur. (swelling of lymphatics) ; Nitr. ac., Sulphur. (swollen glands).
Compatible : Arnic. (contusions) ; Arsen. (cancer) ; Bellad. (incipient amaurosis, cerebro-spinal irritation, cancer) ; Calcar. (scrofula, lymphatic enlargement) ; Droser. (pertussis) ; Lycop., Nux vom., Phosphor., Pulsat., Rhus tox. (contusions) ; Stramon. (sexual debility).
Wine and spirits often improve the sick who require Conium, though it suits persons who cannot take alcoholic stimulants.
Compare : Arnic., Arsen., Bar. carb. (lymphatic swellings) ; Bellad., Calcar., Cicut., Coffea, Droser., Dulcam., Lycop., Mag. mur., Mercur., Nitr. ac., Nitr. spir. dulc., Nux vom., Phosphor., Pulsat., Rhus tox., Stramon., Sulphur, Valer.
